purpose: Standardises reporting of coronary artery calcium, with a risk statement and management recommendations, on dedicated calcium-score scans and on any non-contrast chest CT, whatever the indication.
exam: dedicated CT coronary artery calcium scan, or non-contrast chest CT in which coronary calcium is assessed
system: CAC-DRS: Coronary Artery Calcium Data and Reporting System
aliases: coronary artery calcium data and reporting system

inputs.label: Agatston score
inputs.how_stated: the total coronary Agatston calcium score as a number, e.g. 'Agatston score 450'. not_assessable when no Agatston score is available (visual estimate only, or only the category dictated).

inputs.label: CAC-DRS category
inputs.how_stated: the category digit 0 to 3 as dictated, e.g. 'CAC-DRS 2' or 'CAC-DRS V2/N3' (the digit after the A or V scoring-system letter; ignore the /N vessel count). Used when no Agatston score is available.

summary.text: CAC-DRS is the SCCT 2018 consensus reporting system for coronary artery calcium on non-contrast CT. It applies to all dedicated CAC scans and to all non-gated non-contrast chest CT, irrespective of the indication, and gives one category from 0 to 3 per patient with a risk statement.

The category comes from the total Agatston score, or from a visual none/mild/moderate/severe estimate on non-gated scans. The category carries the same meaning either way, but the scoring system used should be documented.

Two modifiers are reported: A (Agatston) or V (visual), and N, the number of vessels with calcium (1 to 4). N is prognostically additive to the total score, but data are insufficient to change the category on it; it may influence how aggressively management is pursued. N is not used for category 0.
Examples are written CAC-DRS A0, A1/N3, A2/N3, A3/N4 and V0, V1/N3, V2/N3, V3/N4.

In the source, CAC is used to inform a discussion between clinician and patient about the likelihood of net benefit from preventive therapy. The management lines in the US reference table below are general recommendations of that discussion, not instructions.

definitions.text: Category 1: Agatston 1-99, or visual mild. Mildly increased risk.

locator.table: Table 1 a. Agatston Score; b. Visual Score

definitions.text: Category 2: Agatston 100-299, or visual moderate. Moderately increased risk.

locator.table: Table 1 a. Agatston Score; b. Visual Score

definitions.text: Category 3: Agatston 300 or above (printed '> 300'; the text gives 300-1000 and above 1000 as one combined category), or visual severe. Moderately to severely increased risk.

The Agatston score is a summed score from calcified plaque area and the peak density of each calcified lesion. It may be applied to gated and non-gated studies acquired at 120 kV with 2.5-3 mm slices; age, sex and ethnicity percentiles are also routinely reported.

Visual score: 0 none, 1 mild, 2 moderate, 3 severe. It is based on estimating the extent of calcium in each artery, may be used on non-contrast non-gated studies, and gives the same categories 0 to 3.

pitfalls.text: The Agatston bands are printed as 100-299 and '> 300', which leaves exactly 300 unstated; the text's 300-1000 range puts a score of 300 in category 3.
Visual estimation may be used on non-gated non-contrast CT but should not be applied to gated CAC scans.
The vessel modifier N should not be used with category 0.
Aortic, aortic valve, mitral annular and pericardial calcification are reported as none, mild, moderate or severe but are not part of CAC-DRS scoring.

The source frames CAC as ASCVD risk assessment and its management lines as preventive therapy, but states the system applies to all dedicated CAC scans and all non-gated non-contrast chest CT irrespective of indication. It gives no exclusion for known coronary disease or prior infarction, so the pack asks no eligibility question.
